title: A dust temperature limit gives model-dependent mass bounds for 114 TESS complex periodic variables
abstract: We test exposed dust at corotation for 114 complex periodic variables with reported radius and temperature values in TESS sectors 56 to 107. We invert a grain equilibrium model to find the required stellar mass, including the finite angular size of a uniform star. For grey grains limited to 1500 K, three objects require more than 0.8 solar masses at the reported parameters. This count falls to zero when radii are 20% smaller and temperatures are 150 K lower. It is also zero at a temperature limit of 1800 K. At 1500 K, a heating ratio of two raises the count to 21. The result gives conditional tests of the dust model but no robust dust exclusion. Unknown masses, catalogue parameter errors, grain properties, source selection and unresolved companions limit the test. This equilibrium calculation does not measure sublimation rates or material lifetimes. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. Source record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Counts that fail specified thermal and mass limits in 114 selected CPVs. The right panel tests stellar parameter changes. These are conditional model counts, not occurrence estimates or confidence bounds.

citations.reason: Uses verified CPV labels and sector stellar parameters for a thermal feasibility test.
